subject: Discovery: Observability + Evals — success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@finlytics.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery: Observability + Evals — success criteria & next steps

Hi Alice / Rajiv,

Thanks again for carving out time today — great first discussion. Below is a quick post-call recap capturing the pain we heard, measurable success criteria, what you showed us for the current stack, and proposed next steps so we can align on an eval that demonstrates value quickly.

Pain points (as we heard them)
- Hard to detect and roll back quality regressions when model updates are rolled; alerts today are token-rate / latency only.
- No single view correlating prompt variants, model version, and user-facing error / mismatch rates.
- Tracing is ad hoc; engineering has partial hooks into inference but lacks a standard event envelope for prompt/response traces.

Current stack & constraints
- Inference today: managed LLM endpoints via vendor X (batching disabled, high per-token costs).
- Observability: Prometheus + Grafana for infra, custom S3 logs for request/response payloads.
- Security: SOC2 in progress; procurement requires an IP/data handling statement and an audit log export option.

Success criteria (what would make this a win for Finlytics)
1) Detection: Regression alerts that catch >80% of prompt-level quality drops within 15 minutes of rollout.
2) Diagnostics: A dashboard that shows prompt-set level accuracy/entropy and a tracing hook to fetch the exact KV-cache/latency profile for failed examples.
3) Economics: Per-token cost no more than 60% of current managed spend for comparable latency SLAs during ~1k reqs/s steady workload.
4) Security: Audit log delivery and encryption-at-rest compatible with your KMS policy.

Concrete deliverables we propose for the eval
- Golden prompt set: 300 scored prompts + expected outputs (you to share initial set; we can augment).
- Tracing hooks spec: small XLSX we attached (trace-hook-specs.xlsx) detailing the headers/event points we need to instrument.
- Dashboard mockups: PNG attached showing proposed panels for prompt-set drift, per-prompt latencies, and model-variant comparisons (obsv-dashboard-mockup.png).
- Short trial: 2-week eval on a 3-model variant matrix (base / quantized / trimmed context) with regression alerts wired to your PagerDuty test route.

Next steps / asks from Finlytics
- Please confirm the golden prompt owner and share the initial CSV of ~100 canonical prompts by EOD Fri (May 7).
- Confirm whether we should target your Staging cluster or a Redwood Dedicated trial account for the eval.
- Any procurement constraints or non-negotiable contract clauses we should surface early (data residency, IP).

What we'll deliver this week
- Draft mutual action plan (MAP) with timeline and evaluation metrics (I'll send by end of day Thursday).
- A short one-page security/controls note for procurement to accelerate SOC2-adjacent questions.
- Baseline eval plan PDF attached (redwood-eval-plan.pdf).

If that all looks right, can we lock a 30-minute follow-up next Wed (May 12) for MAP review and to confirm golden prompts?

Thanks again — excited to dig in.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

One more ask: can you include an example of the regression alert rule (pseudo-code or threshold examples)? That will help us scope notification noise.

I'll confirm a follow-up cadence after I sync with Rajiv. For now tentative: Wed May 12 11:00 AM PT works.

On a practical note: we cannot share production data into external evals; we'll provide anonymized records for the golden prompts. Is that acceptable?

Thanks — noted and few practical notes from the Solutions team: 

- Regression alert example: we typically start with a two-tier rule:
  * Rule A (fast, noisy): rolling 10-minute window; if prompt-set A accuracy drops by >= 15% vs baseline AND average response entropy increases by > 0.3, fire a P3 alert into Slack/PagerDuty.
  * Rule B (confidence): 60-minute aggregated delta >= 12% and user-visible failure rate increase > 0.5%, fire P1 to on-call and trigger an automated canary rollback if the release was within last 45 minutes.
  (We'll provide these as YAML snippets in the MAP.)

- Rollout guardrails we recommend for the eval: canary at 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback threshold tied to Rule B. We'll include sample traffic-shift configs.

- For the Dedicated trial: we'll provision a non-prod Dedicated slice that mirrors your production GPU class. Can you confirm approximate peak concurrency (reqs/s) and target p99 latency under 3s? That will determine instance sizing.

I've uploaded a draft MAP and the trace hook spec to the shared Drive (link below). I'll also prepare the YAML for alerting and a small sample of the golden prompt scoring template.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
